html:
Galicia-Volhynia was a medieval state in what is now western Ukraine and nearby lands, from 1199 to 1349. It was one of the three strongest states to emerge from Kievan Rus', and it is on the map for 1200.

Roman the Great joined the principalities of Galicia and Volhynia in 1199. His son Daniel fought for decades to hold them against Hungarian and Polish rivals and his own nobles. When the Mongols came he had to submit to the Golden Horde, but in 1253 he took a crown from a papal envoy and became King of Rus. He founded Lviv, named after his son Lev.

The state lay between the Catholic west and the Orthodox east and traded with both. When its ruling line died out in the 1340s, Poland took Galicia and Lithuania took Volhynia.
